steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on a Farsi-language mental health chatbot based on the Self-Attachment Technique (SAT). It should motivate the need in Iran and other Farsi-speaking regions, explain SAT and earlier digital SAT platforms, describe what our chatbot does and how we evaluated it, and end with our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Motivation: anxiety and depression after COVID-19, especially in Iran
2. Digital tools and chatbots for mental health; first Farsi chatbot; other Farsi/Dari-speaking regions
3. Self-Attachment Technique (SAT): what it is and how it works
4. Evidence for SAT and prior digital SAT platforms
5. Our system: extending the English SAT chatbot, modules, usability features, evaluation
6. Main contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Motivation
- WHO: anxiety + depression prevalence up 25% globally after COVID-19 pandemic
- Iran among most affected countries in Middle Eastern region; high infection + mortality rates
- previous research in Iran: more anxiety/depression across age and socio-economic groups; causes = trauma of pandemic, social isolation from long quarantines

2. Digital tools / chatbots
- this paper: Farsi chatbot to enhance mental health
- digital tech investigated as supplement to traditional therapy sessions; esp. middle-income countries where mental health professional not always accessible
- chatbots proven effective at easing mental disorders; high user satisfaction
- leading example: Woebot, delivers Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), available + evaluated since 2017 for English speakers worldwide
- to our knowledge first mental health chatbot in Persian (Farsi) - official language in Iran, spoken by tens of millions of others in Middle East
- also Afghanistan: Dari (sometimes called Farsi) most widely spoken; Farsi and Dari dialects of each other, mutually intelligible in written form
- Afghanistan: anxiety/depression rose during pandemic; lacks therapeutic infrastructure
- Farsi also spoken in Tajikistan, some northern/western parts of Pakistan, southern parts of Persian Gulf

3. SAT
- recently developed psychotherapy framework based on attachment theory (main paradigm in developmental psychology) + interdisciplinary concepts: neuroscience, neuroplasticity, mathematical models, artificial neural networks
- user builds compassionate connection, then internal affectional bond, between 'adult self' (logical, reasoning) and 'childhood self' (emotional), represented by favorite childhood photo or avatar from it
- aims to optimize emotion regulation circuits
- positive interaction with childhood self moderates arousal; minimizes negative emotions (anxiety, depression), maximizes positive ones
- impact of protocols captured by mathematical model based on Hopfield network (one of first artificial models of associative memory)
- computational models of the brain also support SAT protocol

4. Evidence + prior platforms
- effective in clinical and non-clinical populations
- considerable effect size in three-month pilot study, chronically depressed and anxious women in Iran
- 26 self-administered exercises for emotional self-regulation and well-being; self-administered -> suits digital delivery
- Alazraki et al.: new dataset + computational strategy for digital coach guiding SAT practice; identify underlying emotions, human-like characters for engagement
- VR platform for SAT evaluated: participants rate immersion, learnability, overall usability -> promising
- high-end VR version on Oculus Quest suggests SAT exercises based on user sentiment
- low-end version on Google Cardboard: large effect sizes for compassion + well-being, 8-week pilot, non-clinical population

5. Our system
- extends existing text-only English SAT chatbot
- large pool of Farsi utterances via reinforcement learning with ParsGPT-2; similar to approach for translating English utterances into Standard Chinese
- select most coherent utterance at each stage using ParsBERT embeddings
- mix of model-based and rule-based modules for sentiment and intent
- emotion recognition: trained on dataset of over 6,000 examples we collected, 12 fine-grained emotions, 92.13% accuracy
- usability: text + voice, cross-platform, option to switch tone formal/informal
- QA system SAT Teacher answers questions about SAT
- human study, N=51 non-clinical volunteers; most rate chatbot highly on all metrics, overall average 7.25 on 1-10 scale; SAT Teacher average 7.42

6. Contributions
- (1) Farsi chatbot for mental health; first mental health chatbot in Farsi as far as we know
- (2) monolingual Farsi datasets collected, public on GitHub; good monolingual data fundamental to moving Farsi from low to high-resource language
- (3) effectiveness tested in non-clinical population, N=51; paves way for future clinical studies

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The World Health Organization says that the prevalence of anxiety and depression went up by 25% globally after the COVID-19 pandemic. Iran was one of the countries in the Middle Eastern region that was most affected by COVID-19, and it had high infection rates and high mortality rates. Previous research has found that levels of anxiety and depression went up in Iran across different age groups and socio-economic groups, and this is attributed to the trauma of the pandemic and to the social isolation caused by long quarantine periods.

In this paper we develop a Farsi chatbot to enhance mental health. Digital technologies have been investigated a lot as a possible tool to supplement traditional therapy sessions, especially in middle-income countries where people cannot always get access to a mental health professional. Chatbots in particular have been proven to be effective at easing mental disorders, and they have been shown to get high levels of user satisfaction. A leading example is the Woebot platform, which delivers Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) and has been available and evaluated since 2017 for English-speaking populations around the world. As far as we know, our chatbot is the first chatbot for mental health in Persian, which is also called Farsi. Farsi is the official language in Iran and it is spoken by tens of millions of other people in the Middle East. A Farsi chatbot could also help mental health interventions in Afghanistan, where the most widely spoken language is Dari, which is sometimes called Farsi. Farsi and Dari are dialects of each other and they are mutually intelligible in written form. In Afghanistan the incidence of anxiety and depression has gone up during the pandemic, and the country does not have the right therapeutic infrastructure to deal with the issue. Farsi is also spoken in Tajikistan, in some of the northern and western parts of Pakistan, and in the southern parts of the Persian Gulf.

Our dialogue agent is based on the Self-Attachment Technique (SAT), which is a recently developed psychotherapy framework. SAT is based on attachment theory, which is a main paradigm in developmental psychology, and on several interdisciplinary concepts like neuroscience, neuroplasticity, mathematical models, and artificial neural networks. The technique helps the user to first create a compassionate connection and then an internal affectional bond between their 'adult self', which is the logical and reasoning self, and their 'childhood self', which is the emotional self. The childhood self is represented by the user's favorite childhood photo or by an avatar made from this photo. The aim is to optimize emotion regulation circuits. Interacting positively with the childhood self moderates arousal levels, so negative emotions like anxiety and depression are minimized and positive emotions are maximized. The impact of the Self-Attachment protocols can be captured with a mathematical model based on the Hopfield network, which was one of the first artificial models of associative memory. There are also computational models of the brain that support the SAT protocol.

SAT has been shown to be effective in clinical and non-clinical populations. It had a considerable effect size in a three-month pilot study with chronically depressed and anxious women in Iran. SAT has 26 self-administered exercises that users do to enhance their emotional self-regulation and well-being. Because it is self-administered, SAT is well suited to being delivered digitally. Alazraki et al. present a new dataset and a computational strategy for a digital coach that guides people practicing SAT. They identify underlying emotions and create human-like characters to get high engagement in the virtual therapy sessions. Also, a VR platform for SAT was developed and evaluated by asking participants to rate how immersive, learnable and usable overall the platform was, and the results were promising. A high-end implementation of this VR platform, which uses Oculus Quest, suggests suitable SAT exercises based on the user's sentiment. A low-end implementation using Google Cardboard showed large effect sizes for enhancing compassion and well-being in an 8-week pilot study in the non-clinical population.

- Our system
  - extends existing text-only English SAT chatbot
  - Farsi utterance pool via reinforcement learning with ParsGPT-2 (similar to English -> Standard Chinese approach)
  - most coherent utterance per stage chosen with ParsBERT embeddings
  - model-based + rule-based modules for sentiment and intent
  - emotion recognition: over 6,000 collected examples, 12 fine-grained emotions, 92.13% accuracy
  - text + voice, cross-platform, formal/informal tone option
  - SAT Teacher QA system
  - human study N=51 non-clinical; overall average 7.25 on 1-10 scale; SAT Teacher 7.42
- Contributions
  - (1) first mental health chatbot in Farsi
  - (2) monolingual Farsi datasets public on GitHub; needed to move Farsi from low to high-resource
  - (3) tested with N=51 non-clinical participants -> future clinical studies

steps.text:
According to the World Health Organization, the prevalence of anxiety and depression increased by 25% globally after the COVID-19 pandemic [1]. Iran was among the countries in the Middle Eastern region most affected by COVID-19 [2,3], with high infection and mortality rates [4,5]. Previous research has recorded increased levels of anxiety and depression across different age and socio-economic groups in Iran, attributed to the trauma of the pandemic and the social isolation caused by long quarantine periods [6,7,8,9].

In this paper, we develop a Farsi chatbot to enhance mental health. Digital technologies have been widely investigated as a possible tool for supplementing traditional therapy sessions [10], especially in middle-income countries where access to a mental health professional may not always be possible [11]. Chatbots in particular have been proven effective at easing mental disorders [12,13] and have been shown to reach high levels of user satisfaction [14,15,16]. As a leading example, the Woebot platform, which delivers Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), has been available and evaluated since 2017 for English-speaking populations around the world [17]. To our knowledge, this is the first chatbot for mental health in Persian, also called Farsi, which is the official language in Iran and is spoken by tens of millions of other people in the Middle East [18]. A Farsi-speaking chatbot could also help mental health interventions in Afghanistan, where Dari, sometimes called Farsi, is the most widely spoken language. Farsi and Dari are dialects of each other and are mutually intelligible in written form. The incidence of anxiety and depression in Afghanistan has risen during the pandemic [19,20], and the country lacks the therapeutic infrastructure to address the issue [21]. Farsi is also spoken in Tajikistan, some northern and western parts of Pakistan, and the southern parts of the Persian Gulf [22].

Our dialogue agent is grounded in the Self-Attachment Technique (SAT) [23,24], a recently developed psychotherapy framework based on attachment theory, a main paradigm in developmental psychology, and on several interdisciplinary concepts such as neuroscience, neuroplasticity, mathematical models, and artificial neural networks [24]. The technique helps the user create first a compassionate connection and then an internal affectional bond between their ‘adult self’ (the logical and reasoning self) and their ‘childhood self’ (the emotional self), represented by the user’s favorite childhood photo or an avatar created from this photo. This scheme aims to optimize emotion regulation circuits. By interacting positively with the childhood self, the technique moderates arousal levels, minimizing negative emotions such as anxiety and depression and maximizing positive emotions. The impact of Self-Attachment protocols can be captured with a mathematical model based on the Hopfield network, one of the first artificial models of associative memory [23]. Computational models of the brain also support the SAT protocol [25,26].

SAT has proven effective in both clinical and non-clinical populations [27,28], and showed a considerable effect size in a three-month pilot study in a population of chronically depressed and anxious women in Iran [29]. SAT consists of 26 self-administered exercises for users to enhance their emotional self-regulation and well-being. Because it is self-administered, SAT lends itself well to digital delivery [30,31,32]. Alazraki et al. present a new dataset and a computational strategy for a digital coach that guides experimenters in practicing SAT; they identify underlying emotions and craft human-like characters to achieve high engagement in the virtual therapy sessions [33]. In addition, a VR platform for SAT has been developed and evaluated by asking participants to rate its level of immersion, learnability, and overall usability, with promising results [30]. A high-end implementation of this VR platform, using Oculus Quest, suggests appropriate SAT exercises according to the user’s sentiment [31]. A low-end implementation using Google Cardboard has shown large effect sizes for enhancing compassion and well-being in an 8-week pilot study in the non-clinical population [32].

Our work extends an existing text-only SAT chatbot in English [33] by creating a large pool of Farsi utterances with a reinforcement learning approach using ParsGPT-2 [34], similar to the approach explored in [35] for translating English utterances into Standard Chinese. At each stage of the conversation, we then select the most coherent utterance from the dataset using ParsBERT [36] embeddings. Our chatbot also relies on a mixture of model-based and rule-based modules to understand user sentiment and intent. Our emotion recognition module, trained on a dataset of over 6,000 examples that we collected, identifies 12 fine-grained emotions with 92.13% accuracy.

To maximize usability, our chatbot supports both text-based and voice-based modalities, is cross-platform, and lets users change the tone of the conversation from formal to informal. Finally, we add to the platform a QA system called SAT Teacher that answers user questions about SAT. We evaluated the chatbot in a human study with N=51 volunteers from the non-clinical population. The majority of participants rate the chatbot highly on all metrics (overall average score of 7.25 on a 1-10 scale). The SAT teacher also scores positively (average score 7.42).

Our main contributions are: (1) We developed a Farsi chatbot to enhance mental health; to the best of our knowledge, it is the first mental health chatbot in Farsi; (2) we collected monolingual Farsi datasets and made them publicly available on GitHub, since good-quality monolingual datasets are fundamental for moving Farsi from a low to a high-resource language [37]; (3) we examined the effectiveness of the chatbot in a non-clinical population with N=51 participants, paving the way for future clinical studies applying similar technologies.
